resources.string: Could not add backgrounds. Your current background is unchanged.
Import stopped. Any copies already added are kept.
Select one or more photos, up to 32 MB each. Tap Use to show a saved photo on Stage. Your original files stay unchanged.
Select one or more videos, up to 512 MB and six hours each. Tap Use to show a saved video on Stage without sound. Your original files stay unchanged.
While using a video background, KANTA can switch to a different built-in or imported video when a song starts.
Tap Use on an imported photo first. KANTA can switch to a different imported photo when a song starts.
Use a different background before removing this copy.
You can select several files at once. KANTA keeps copies and leaves your originals unchanged.
Add an MP3 or WAV in Menu → Intermission or Menu → Presets first. Your original file stays unchanged.
On · Waiting for karaoke to finish
Choose one track to loop between songs. Imports also appear in Presets and can be used in Menu → Party Pads.

1. Tap Add MP3 or WAV and select one or more files.
2. Find a track in Imported tracks and tap Use. Only one track is selected at a time.
3. Turn on between-song music and set Between-song volume. Your track loops when no karaoke song is loaded. It stops while a song is starting or loaded, or when you leave the app.

KANTA welcome plays once when the stage is idle. Switching back to it does not replay it if it already played.

Tap a pad to play its sound. To use your own sound, add an MP3 or WAV in Intermission or Presets, then tap Assign clip beside a pad. Clips must be mono or stereo, up to 30 seconds and 8 MB. Tap Reset to restore that pad’s original sound. Party sound volume is separate from the music volume.

Before removing a track, select a different track or KANTA welcome, and reset any pads that use it in Menu → Party Pads. Removing the copy also removes it from Presets, Up Next, and saved playlists. Your original stays unchanged.
Use another track or KANTA welcome, or reset any pads using this track, before removing the copy.
